heroData.title: Hire in Japan Without Entity
heroData.subtitle: EOR vs Haken (Dispatch)
heroData.description: Rapidly deploy staff in Tokyo. EOR ensures Shakai Hoken (Social Insurance) compliance and handles 36 Agreement filings.

steps.title: Offer Letter
steps.description: Naitei Sho (Offer of Employment) issued detailing core terms.

steps.title: Rules of Emp.
steps.description: Shugyo Kisoku (Work Rules) must be provided to the employee.

steps.title: Social Ins.
steps.description: Enrollment in Shakai Hoken (Pension/Health) within 5 days of start.

steps.title: My Number
steps.description: Collection of 12-digit Social Security/Tax ID (My Number) for tax filing.

steps.title: 36 Agreement
steps.description: EOR files Article 36 Agreement to allow overtime work.

rows.label: Management Fee
values: Monthly per employee. Includes payroll and admin.

rows.label: Onboarding Fee
values: One-time per employee for setup and registration.

items.title: Termination Risk
items.text: Extremely difficult in Japan. PIPs (Performance Improvement Plans) must be genuine and documented over 3-6 months to withstand court scrutiny.

items.title: Bonuses (Shoyo)
items.text: Typically 2-4 months of pay. Not legally mandatory but culturally expected. EORs must facilitate these payments.

items.title: 36 Agreement
items.text: Mandatory filing to allow any overtime. EOR typically handles this as the legal employer of record.

faqs.question: Can I use EOR for solo freelancers?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it effectively converts them to employees. For true freelance, use 'Gyomu Itaku' (Service Agreement) instead.

faqs.question: Who owns the IP?
faqs.answer: The client. EOR contracts strictly transfer all work product rights to the client company.

faqs.question: Is insurance provided?
faqs.answer: Yes, statutory health and workers' comp are included. Supplemental life/dental can be added for extra fee.

faqs.question: Can EOR sponsor a visa?
faqs.answer: Many EORs can sponsor 'Engineer/Specialist in Humanities' visas for their employees.

items.title: Nominication
items.text: Workplace bonding through drinking ('Nomikai') is common and often seen as essential for team harmony.

items.title: Seishain Status
items.text: Most prestigious employment status. Offers indefinite term and maximum legal protection.

items.title: Meishi (Business Cards)
items.text: Exchange with two hands, bow slightly. Treat the card with respect (don't write on it or pocket it immediately).

items.title: Keigo (Honorifics)
items.text: Levels of politeness (Sonkeigo, Kenjougo, Teineigo) are crucial in B2B communication.

items.title: Nomikai
items.text: Drinking parties are key for team bonding ('Nominication'). Attendance is often expected.

items.title: Omiyage
items.text: Souvenirs/Gifts from trips are customary to share with the office team.

items.title: Haken (Dispatch)
items.text: Temporary staffing where the worker is employed by the agency but works at the client site. Strictly regulated.

items.title: Seishain (Permanent)
items.text: Regular full-time employee with indefinite contract term. Very high job security.

items.title: Shugyo Kisoku
items.text: Rules of Employment. Mandatory for companies with >10 employees to define working conditions.

items.title: MHLW Labor Standards
items.text: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare guide to labor laws.

items.title: JETRO Investing in Japan
items.text: Comprehensive guide for setting up business and employment in Japan.

steps.title: Cut-off
steps.description: Attendance data finalized (e.g., 20th of month).

steps.title: Calculation
steps.description: Gross Pay - (Shakai Hoken + Income Tax + Resident Tax) = Net Pay.

steps.title: Payday
steps.description: Usually 25th of the current month. Paid via bank transfer (Furikomi).

steps.title: Tax Pay
steps.description: Withheld Income Tax remitted by 10th of following month.

steps.title: Insurance Pay
steps.description: Social Insurance premiums remitted by end of following month.

items.title: Resident Tax Deficit
items.text: New arrivals pay ¥0 in Year 1. Year 2 bills are huge as they reflect Year 1 income. Warn employees to save.

items.title: Commuting Exemption
items.text: Up to ¥150k/mo is tax-free. Ensure this is separate from base pay to reduce tax burden.

items.title: Year-End Tax (Nenmatsu Chosei)
items.text: Employer reconciles tax in Dec. Most employees don't need to file individual returns.

faqs.question: When is payday?
faqs.answer: 90% of Japanese firms pay on the 25th. If a holiday, it moves earlier to the 24th or 23rd.

faqs.question: Can we pay in USD?
faqs.answer: Only if the employee agrees and the contract explicitly allows, but they still need JPY for local expenses/taxes.

faqs.question: How are bonuses taxed?
faqs.answer: Taxed at source, but the bracket is based on previous month's regular salary.

items.title: Nencho
items.text: Short for Nenmatsu Chosei. The massive Dec admin cycle of collecting life insurance certificates.

items.title: NTA Withholding Tax Guide
items.text: National Tax Agency's English guide for withholding income tax.

steps.title: Commuting Allowance Optimization
steps.description: Separate the commuting allowance from base pay. In Japan, it's tax-exempt up to ¥150,000/month, reducing both employee tax and employer social insurance.

steps.title: Social Insurance Enrollment
steps.description: Verify that all employees (including 3/4-time staff) are enrolled in Health Insurance and Welfare Pension. This adds approx. 15.5% to your base salary cost.

steps.title: Overtime Cap Configuration
steps.description: Set up '36 Agreement' alerts in your payroll system. Monitor overtime hours against the 45h/month and 360h/year statutory caps to avoid criminal penalties.

items.title: Resident Tax (Inhabitant)
items.text: Typically 10% (6% city, 4% pref). Usually paid in arrears based on previous year's income. New arrivals don't pay in year 1.

items.title: Social Insurance
items.text: Employer pays approx. 15.5% on top of base salary for Pension, Health, and Unemployment insurance.

items.title: Commuting Allowance
items.text: Tax-exempt up to ¥150,000/month. Standard benefit for almost all Japan employees.

faqs.question: What is the 'Bonus' system?
faqs.answer: Commonly 2-4 months of salary paid twice a year. While not mandatory, it is a strong cultural expectation.

faqs.question: How are overtime (Zangyo) rates calculated?
faqs.answer: Minimum 25% premium for overtime (>40h/week), 35% for holiday work, and 25% for late-night work (22:00-05:00).

faqs.question: What is 'Minashi Zangyo'?
faqs.answer: Fixed overtime pay. A set number of hours (e.g., 20 or 40) is included in the base salary. Any excess must still be paid.

items.title: Year-end Adjustment
items.text: Employers perform 'Nenmatsu Chosei' in December to settle the exact annual tax for employees, often resulting in a small tax refund.

items.title: Labor Insurance
items.text: Annual labor insurance reporting is done in July (Rodo Hoken), reconciling estimated vs actual premiums.

items.title: My Number System
items.text: Employers must collect and manage 'My Number' (Individual Number) for all employees for tax and social insurance purposes under strict security.

heroData.title: Setup KK or GK
heroData.subtitle: Kabushiki Kaisha vs Godo Kaisha
heroData.description: KK (Stock Company) is prestigious, preferred by big clients. GK (LLC) is cheaper, faster, becoming popular (e.g., Apple Japan GK).

steps.title: Articles
steps.description: Draft Articles of Incorporation (Teikan). Define scope, year-end, directors.

steps.title: Capital
steps.description: Deposit paid-in capital (min ¥1) into a personal bank account in Japan.

steps.title: Notary (KK only)
steps.description: Notarization of Articles required for KK (~¥50k). Not required for GK.

steps.title: Registry
steps.description: File application with Legal Affairs Bureau (Houmukyoku). Company born this day.

steps.title: Post-Setup
steps.description: Notify Tax Office, Labor Office, Pension Office, and Bank of Japan.

items.title: Bank Account Hurdle
items.text: Even after registry, bank accounts take 1-3 months and are frequently rejected for foreign firms without a resident director.

items.title: Hanko (Seal) Custom
items.text: Despite digitization efforts, the Representative Seal (Jitsuin) is still legally required for most binding contracts.

items.title: Paid-in Capital
items.text: While ¥1 is the legal minimum, ¥5M is recommended for Business Manager visa eligibility and bank credibility.

faqs.question: Can I use a virtual office?
faqs.answer: For registration, yes. For bank accounts and visas, usually no. Banks expect a physical desk and sign.

faqs.question: Do I need a resident director?
faqs.answer: Legally no, but practically yes for banking and certain licenses.

faqs.question: What is the tax year-end?
faqs.answer: In Japan, you choose. Many foreign firms use Dec 31, while domestic firms use March 31.

items.title: Tax Notifications
items.text: Must notify the National Tax Agency and local municipality within 1-2 months of founding.

items.title: Social Insurance
items.text: Corporate entities must enroll in Shakai Hoken immediately upon hiring the first director or employee.

items.title: Legal Affairs Bureau
items.text: Where corporate registrations are filed (website in Japanese often required for forms).

items.title: JETRO Setting Up
items.text: Procedures for incorporating a company in Japan.

heroData.title: Recruitment Agencies
heroData.subtitle: Bilingual Talent
heroData.description: Fierce competition for bilingual (Jap/Eng) staff. Fees are high. 'Shokugyo ANtei Jo' (Hello Work) is the public option.

steps.title: JD & Benchmarking
steps.description: Draft bilingual Job Description. Benchmark salary against market (typically 20-30% higher for bilingual roles).

steps.title: Sourcing & Screening
steps.description: Leverage agencies (Direct Search) and platforms like LinkedIn/Wantedly. Initial HR filter for cultural fit.

steps.title: Multi-stage Interviews
steps.description: Typically 3 rounds: Functional Lead, Japan Country Manager, and Regional/HQ Head. Consensus-based hiring is common.

steps.title: Reference Checks
steps.description: Standard practice in Japan. Verification of previous employment and performance.

steps.title: Offer (Naitei)
steps.description: Verbal offer followed by 'Naitei Sho' (Offer of Employment). Candidate confirms resignation from current firm.

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Collection of Pension Book, Tax ID, and bank account details for Shakai Hoken setup.

rows.label: Contingent Search
values: Payable only upon successful hire and start date.

rows.label: Temp-to-Perm
values: Fee paid after trial period (usually 3-6 months).

rows.label: Job Boards
values: Flat fee for 4-week posting (e.g., BizReach, Wantedly).

items.title: Bilingual Premium
items.text: English fluency (TOEIC 800+) adds a significant premium to base salaries, often making Japan talent 40% more expensive than local-only peers.

items.title: BizReach Dominance
items.text: BizReach is the premier platform for high-income professionals in Japan. Most Top-tier agencies source here rather than LinkedIn.

items.title: Job Change Stigma
items.text: While decreasing, 'Kojin-Jigyo' (freelance) or frequent job changes (>4 in 10 years) can still be scrutinized by conservative Japanese firms.

faqs.question: What is 'Hello Work' and is it useful?
faqs.answer: Hello Work is the government's free job-matching service. While free, it is rarely effective for high-level bilingual talent and is mostly used for blue-collar or entry-level administrative roles.

faqs.question: How do recruiters handle the 'resignation' period?
faqs.answer: Most permanent contracts require 30 days' notice. Recruiters often coach candidates on how to handle 'resignation pressure' from current managers, which is common in Japan.

faqs.question: Are background checks legal in Japan?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they must comply with the Personal Information Protection Act (APPI). Consent is mandatory, and criminal record checks are highly restricted.

items.title: Shokai
items.text: Refers to the introduction or placement of a candidate by an agency.

items.title: Naitei
items.text: The unofficial-but-binding job offer. Once Naitei is given, withdrawing it is legally difficult for the employer.

items.title: Rirekisho & Shokumu Keirekisho
items.text: Standard Japanese resume formats. Rirekisho is personal/educational; Shokumu Keirekisho is professional experience.

heroData.title: HR Tech (SaaS)
heroData.subtitle: SmartHR & Freee
heroData.description: Domestic platforms like SmartHR dominate for Social Insurance paperwork digitization.

steps.title: Platform Selection & Needs Analysis
steps.description: Evaluate local SaaS leaders (SmartHR, Freee, Money Forward) against your headcount and existing accounting software. Focus on e-filing capabilities for social insurance.

steps.title: Social Insurance Digitization
steps.description: Connect the HRIS to government portals for paperless submission of Health Insurance and Employee Pension paperwork. Reduces admin time by 60%.

steps.title: My Number Security Isolation
steps.description: Configure the HRIS to strictly control access to employee 'My Number' data. Ensure audit logs are active to comply with Japanese PIPA (APPI) regulations.

items.title: Global HRIS Gap
items.text: Global platforms (Workday, BambooHR) often lack direct e-filing for Japanese social insurance. Middleware or local add-ons are required.

items.title: Attendance Tracking
items.text: Strict labor laws require precise tracking of login/logout times. Choose a system that supports Japanese '36 Agreement' alerts.

items.title: My Number Security
items.text: Systems must strictly isolate My Number data with access logs to comply with Japanese privacy laws.

faqs.question: Can SmartHR replace a payroll vendor?
faqs.answer: It automates the data collection and filing, but many firms still use a payroll specialist to verify the final calculations for edge cases.

faqs.question: Does it support English?
faqs.answer: SmartHR has limited English UI. For global firms, Money Forward Cloud often offers better multilingual support options.

items.title: Kintai Kanri
items.text: The management of working hours, and the most common first step in HR digitization in Japan.

items.title: Denshi Shinsei
items.text: Digital applications to government offices, now standard for large Japanese corporations.

items.title: Digital Agency
items.text: Government agency overseeing digital transformation (DX) and My Number systems.

heroData.title: Tax Accountant (Zeirishi)
heroData.subtitle: Bookkeeping & Tax
heroData.description: Only a licensed Zeirishi can file corporate tax. Double-entry bookkeeping required.

steps.title: Boki (Bookkeeping)
steps.description: Daily entry of receipts and invoices. Can be handled by in-house staff or a Boki specialist.

steps.title: Zeirishi Review
steps.description: Licensed Tax Accountant must review the books (typically monthly or quarterly) for tax compliance.

steps.title: Kessan (Closing)
steps.description: Annual settlement of accounts. The Zeirishi prepares the final corporate tax return based on these audited books.

items.title: Blue Form Election
items.text: Essential for 10-year loss carry-forward. Must apply within 3 months of founding or start of fiscal year.

items.title: Language Barrier
items.text: Most small Zeirishi offices only work in Japanese. English-speaking firms charge a 'Foreign Entity Premium' (typically 1.5x - 2x standard rates).

items.title: Fiscal Year End
items.text: Companies can choose any month. Avoiding the March 31 rush (standard for Japan) can lead to better service from accountants.

faqs.question: Can I do my own corporate taxes?
faqs.answer: Legally yes, but practically impossible. The forms are extremely complex and banks/authorities expect a Zeirishi's official stamp (Inkan) on the return.

faqs.question: What software should I use?
faqs.answer: Freee and Money Forward are the cloud leaders. Traditional firms may still use Yayoi.

items.title: J-GAAP vs IFRS
items.text: Standard SMEs use J-GAAP. Listed companies or subsidiaries of global firms may use IFRS or US GAAP.

items.title: Statutory Audit
items.text: Only required for 'Large Companies' (Capital > ¥500M or Liabilities > ¥20B).

steps.title: 36 Agreement
steps.description: Filed annually with Labor Standards Inspection Office. Essential for any overtime work.

steps.title: Work Rules (Shugyo Kisoku)
steps.description: Mandatory for 10+ employees. Must include leave, pay, and disciplinary policies.

steps.title: Health Check (Kenko Shindan)
steps.description: Company-paid annual medical exams for all full-time employees.

items.title: Black Companies
items.text: The government aggressively labels firms as 'Black' (Burakku Kigyo) if they violate labor laws, destroying recruitment brand value.

items.title: Stress Check
items.text: Mandatory for firms with 50+ employees. Designed to prevent mental health issues from overwork (Karoshi).

items.title: Equal Pay
items.text: Strict 'Equal Pay for Equal Work' laws since 2021 prohibit unreasonable gaps between regular and non-regular employees.

faqs.question: Can I use 'Fixed Overtime' pay?
faqs.answer: Yes (Minashi Zangyo), but it must be clearly stated in the contract with the number of hours included. Any excess must still be paid.

faqs.question: Are foreign firms exempt?
faqs.answer: Absolutely not. The Labor Standards Bureau treats foreign firms the same as domestic ones.

items.title: Labor Standards Act
items.text: Sets minimum conditions for wages, hours, and rest.

items.title: Industrial Safety & Health
items.text: Governs workplace safety and the mandatory health check system.

items.title: Labor Contract Act
items.text: Governs the formation and termination of labor contracts.

items.title: MHLW Working Conditions
items.text: Portal site for workers and employers regarding labor laws.

steps.title: Zeirishi (Tax Accountant) Selection
steps.description: Engage a licensed Japanese Tax Accountant (Zeirishi) early. They are legally required to sign off on corporate tax returns in Japan.

steps.title: Blue Form Tax Return Election
steps.description: File the 'Blue Form' tax return application within 3 months of incorporation. This is essential for 10-year loss carry-forward benefits.

steps.title: JCT Invoice Registration
steps.description: Register for the Japanese Consumption Tax (JCT) Invoice System to allow your business customers to claim tax credits on your invoices.

items.title: Invoice System (Oct 2023)
items.text: To claim JCT credits, sellers must be registered as 'Qualified Invoice Issuers'. This has increased tax burdens for small freelancers.

items.title: Prefectural Variations
items.text: Tokyo has slightly higher inhabitant tax rates than rural areas, but the effective rate difference is usually within 1-2%.

items.title: Withholding (Genzen)
items.text: Companies must withhold tax (typically 10.21%) on payments to individual freelancers and professionals.

faqs.question: What is the filing deadline?
faqs.answer: Within 2 months after the end of the fiscal year.

faqs.question: Are entertainment expenses deductible?
faqs.answer: For SMEs (Capital < ¥100M), up to ¥8 million per year is generally deductible.

items.title: Worldwide Income
items.text: Japanese domestic corporations are taxed on their worldwide income.

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: Japan has strict transfer pricing rules for transactions with foreign affiliates.

heroData.title: Corporate Law
heroData.subtitle: Benshoshi fees
heroData.description: Japanese contracts often vague, relying on long-term trust. English contracts valid but Japanese prevails in court.

steps.title: Employment Rules (Shuoku Kirei)
steps.description: Draft formal 'Work Rules' (Shuoku Kirei). Mandatory for companies with 10+ employees; highly recommended for all to define overtime and leave.

steps.title: Intellectual Property Policy
steps.description: Implement a formal IP transfer policy to comply with Patent Act Article 35, ensuring the company owns employee inventions for 'reasonable remuneration'.

steps.title: Digital Signature Setup
steps.description: Deploy digital signing (CloudSign, DocuSign) to avoid physical 'Inshi' (Stamp Tax) and simplify multi-party contract execution.

rows.label: Hourly Rate (Partner)
values: Tier 1 Tokyo firms. Global firms may charge more.

rows.label: Contract Review
values: Standard MSA or Employment contract review.

rows.label: Dispute Filing
values: Initial filing fee plus success-based percentage.

items.title: Article 35
items.text: Under Japan's Patent Act, employees have an inherent right to 'reasonable remuneration' for inventions. Employers must have a formal policy to transfer these rights.

items.title: Language Hierarchy
items.text: Always stipulate that the Japanese version is the prevailing version for contracts signed in Japan to ensure consistency in court interpretations.

items.title: Stamp Tax (Inshi)
items.text: Physical contracts in Japan require revenue stamps based on the contract value. Digital contracts (e.g., CloudSign) are currently exempt.

faqs.question: Are non-compete clauses enforceable?
faqs.answer: Enforcement is narrow. Courts check if the restriction is necessary to protect trade secrets, the geographical scope, and if the employee was compensated for the restriction.

faqs.question: Is an English signature valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for official government documents (like registry), a registered seal (Jitsuin) or a notarized signature affidavit (for non-residents) is required.

faqs.question: What is 'Gyomu Itaku'?
faqs.answer: It is a service/outsourcing agreement. It is often used for hiring freelancers or external consultants, but misclassification risk is high if you manage them like employees.

items.title: Bengo-shi
items.text: A fully licensed attorney. They can represent clients in any legal matter, including litigation.

items.title: Shiho-shoshi
items.text: Judicial Scrivener. Specialists in corporate registration and real estate filing. Cheaper than attorneys for specific filings.

items.title: Inshi-zei
items.text: Stamp Tax. A mandatory tax paid by affixing 'Inshi' (revenue stamps) to physical contracts.

heroData.title: System Integration
heroData.subtitle: Delivery Models
heroData.description: Unique 'SIer' structure where project liability (Ukeoi) vs effort-based (Jun-inin) contracts define risk.

steps.title: Requirements (Youken Teigi)
steps.description: Heavy focus on defining all 'non-functional' requirements upfront. Alignment with business stakeholders.

steps.title: Basic Design (Kihon Sekkei)
steps.description: User-facing details and overall architecture. Signed off before technical work starts.

steps.title: Detailed Design (Shousai Sekkei)
steps.description: Meticulous internal logic and DB schema documentation. Common in Waterfall models.

steps.title: Development & Unit Test
steps.description: Coding followed by mandatory test evidence collection (screenshots/logs) for every case.

steps.title: Acceptance (Ukeire Test)
steps.description: Formal sign-off by the client. Acceptance triggers payment in 'Ukeoi' contracts.

rows.label: Senior Developer
values: Expert in specific stack (React, Go, AWS). Bilingual premium included.

rows.label: Junior Developer
values: Mid-tier coding skills. Often sourced via SES.

rows.label: Bridge SE
values: Bilingual engineer facilitating offshore team communication.

items.title: Gisou Ukeoi
items.text: Risk of 'false subcontracting' where client gives direct orders to subcontractor's engineers. This is illegal under Labor Dispatch Law.

items.title: Waterfall vs Agile
items.text: Enterprise Japan remains Waterfall-heavy. If using Agile, ensure the 'Jun-inin' contract type is used to avoid fixed-scope liability.

items.title: Security standards
items.text: P-Mark (Privacy Mark) or ISMS certification is often a mandatory prerequisite for vendors handling enterprise data.

faqs.question: What is the standard payment term?
faqs.answer: Typically 'End of current month, pay end of following' (Shime-yoku-getsu-matsu), i.e., net 30 days.

faqs.question: Is insurance needed for IT vendors?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Professional Indemnity' (Baisho Sekinin) insurance is standard to cover system failures or data leaks.

faqs.question: Should we use local server hosting?
faqs.answer: While AWS/Azure (Tokyo Region) is standard, many government/fintech projects still require strictly local data residency.

heroData.title: Agency & Media
heroData.subtitle: Pricing & Strategy
heroData.description: Navigating the 'Kokoku Dairiten' (Agency) landscape from traditional giants to agile digital boutiques.

steps.title: Orientation
steps.description: Briefing the agency on goals, budget, and target audience (KPI definition).

steps.title: Proposal (Kikakusho)
steps.description: Agency presents media mix, creative concepts, and estimated Reach/CTR.

steps.title: Content Localization
steps.description: Not just translation, but 'transcreation' to suit Japanese cultural nuances and aesthetics.

steps.title: Media Buying
steps.description: Booking spots on LINE, Yahoo! Japan, or traditional OOH (Out of Home) media.

steps.title: Optimization
steps.description: Weekly monitoring of performance with monthly reporting (PDCA cycle).

rows.label: Media Commission
values: Standard percentage of the ad spend (Google/SNS/TV).

rows.label: Initial Setup Fee
values: One-time fee for account setup and pixel integration.

rows.label: Monthly Mgmt Fee
values: Flat fee for ongoing optimization (common for small budgets).

rows.label: Creative Production
values: Varies wildly based on video vs static banner sets.

items.title: LINE Supremacy
items.text: LINE is the 'super-app' of Japan. B2C businesses must have a LINE Official Account for engagement.

items.title: Yahoo! Japan
items.text: Unlike the US, Yahoo! Japan (SoftBank) remains a powerful search and display portal, often outperforming Google for certain demographics.

items.title: Creative Density
items.text: Japanese ads often feature higher information density (more text) compared to minimalist Western designs.

faqs.question: Can we use Western influencers?
faqs.answer: Only if your product is aspirational 'Western'. Local 'Talento' or Micro-influencers drive much higher conversion for domestic goods.

faqs.question: What is 'O2O'?
faqs.answer: Online-to-Offline. Strategies involving QR codes or coupons on digital ads to drive foot traffic to physical stores.

faqs.question: Are there ad restrictions for foreign firms?
faqs.answer: Pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and financial ads are strictly regulated by the PMDA or CAA. Compliance checks are mandatory.
